author: partly-wrong
why: Note on གངས་ཅན་པ ('the Himalayans', opponents quoted in Dignāga's Pramāṇasamuccaya, 6th c.) calls them 'a specific school of Tibetan or North Indian logic'. No Tibetan school of logic existed in Dignāga's time; the identification is a hedged guess (the #5624 'relation guess' shape).

author: unverifiable (kept)
why: Mahāvyutpatti gives ཉེ་བར་འཇལ་བ = upamāna, but on this page the term names the 'just as the pot…, so sound' step, i.e. the Nyāya upanaya the note gives; not marked wrong.

author: wrong (kept)
why: ཤེད་ལས་སྐྱེས་པ = manuja/mānava ('born of Manu', 84000 authority entity-1575), not puruṣa; the list also has ཤེད་བུ next.
